solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Male will, as they say, give way

indicators.note: the phrase marks that the words are to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a buck is a male deer, and will shortens in speech to 'll, so male will is spoken as buck'll

explanation.surface: A man of strong will is predicted to yield under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Male will' spoken quickly is 'buck'll', with BUCK a male deer and 'll the contracted will.
explanation.definitionFit: To buckle is to collapse or yield under pressure, a synonym for giving way.

clue.text: Bishop, genuine and hopeful

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
right in the sense of the real, proper or genuine thing

explanation.surface: A churchman described as sincere and optimistic.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright prospects are promising ones, so the word is a synonym for hopeful.

clue.text: Jump around to prune a shrub

parts.note: to cut back a plant is to prune it
the caper is a Mediterranean shrub whose buds are pickled

explanation.surface: A gardener leaps about while trimming a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to skip or frolic about playfully, leaping around.

clue.text: Transport animal heading off carrying black stone and slate

indicators.note: the shortened animal holds the next piece inside it
the animal's first letter is removed, its head taken away

parts.note: the llama is an Andean pack animal used to carry loads
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

explanation.surface: A beast of burden, minus its head, hauls dark rock and roofing slate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' leaves LAMA, which 'carrying' wraps round B to give LAMBA. 'Slate' looks like the stone cargo but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate someone is to criticise them severely, which is exactly what lambasting means.

clue.text: Spooner's low box for key

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two pieces exchange their starts

parts.note: base means low or mean
to spar is to box in practice

explanation.surface: The Reverend's word for a little chest that holds a key.
explanation.walkthrough: BASE SPAR swaps its opening B and SP sounds to give 'space bar'.
explanation.definitionFit: The long bar at the bottom of a keyboard is one of its keys, so it is an example.

clue.text: Exorcist needed to deal with it? Let priest go out

definitions.text: Exorcist needed to deal with it?

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A haunting needs an exorcist, so why is the priest being let go?
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy mischievous spirit is the sort of being an exorcist is called in to drive away.

clue.text: Making money, having lots of it, but not hard at heart

parts.note: a cent is a unit of money

indicators.note: not means the following letter is left out of the word before it

parts.note: someone who has lots of money is rich
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Earning money and having plenty, yet not hard-hearted underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not hard' removes H from RICH to leave RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something centric is central, placed at the core or heart of things.

clue.text: Conservative craft at a high level

definitions.meaning: Colonel ..., a cartoon character, gave his name to a pompous reactionary
a non-rigid airship or barrage balloon floating high in the air

explanation.surface: A Tory vessel operating at senior level.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Blimp was a British cartoon of a pompous, reactionary old officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a reactionary diehard and a small airship that flies high.

clue.text: One good in morris dancing may be following steps precisely

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the rearranged dance word
the letters of morris jig about into a new order

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A capable morris dancer keeps exactly to the steps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' turns MORRIS into RORISM, and 'in' puts IG inside it after the first R.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict adherence to rules is rigorism, a noun for keeping precisely to procedure.

clue.text: Lovey-dovey eventually

definitions.meaning: a borrowing from French for intimate or cosy
in the end, given enough time, read as two words

explanation.surface: Romance will come along in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as one word it is the French for intimate; split, it means sooner or later.

clue.text: Standing by man who has won bakery competition?

definitions.text: man who has won bakery competition?
definitions.meaning: a whimsical title, the king of the custard tarts, split as two words

explanation.surface: Waiting beside the champion of a baking contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To flank is to be at someone's side, as guards stand beside a person.

clue.text: Journalist needing a further restraint …

parts.note: hack is slang for a journalist
further means more, additional

explanation.surface: A reporter wants yet more control.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitless bridle used to control horses is a kind of restraint.

clue.text: Nothing exotic in old books catalogue to engage a student of far-off lands

indicators.note: to engage means to take hold of, so the joined pieces hold the article between them
in puts the foreign word inside the abbreviation for the old books

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the old books of the Bible
rien is French for nothing, exotic meaning foreign
a list is a catalogue

explanation.surface: A catalogue of old books with nothing foreign, though it hires an Asia specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' marks a foreign word, so 'Nothing' is French here, not O. 'to engage' means the joined pieces hold A between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert on the cultures of the East studies distant lands, as the definition says.

clue.text: … that this person might find useful, taking back short account

indicators.note: taking back means the shortened word is read in the reverse direction
short means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a report is an account of events

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a rider who would use the bridle, after a brief account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims REPORT to REPOR before 'taking back' turns it round. The ellipsis ties it to the bridle in 11.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy who lassoes animals would find a bitless bridle handy, so this is the person meant.

clue.text: Communicating what a voter may be doing

definitions.text: what a voter may be doing
definitions.meaning: a voter marks a cross on the ballot paper

explanation.surface: A voter at the booth, getting a message out.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting an idea understood is a synonym for communicating; literally it describes marking an X.

clue.text: Commentators will commentate _______, being tart

definitions.meaning: sports commentators describe events taking place on the field of play
tart is slang for a prostitute, and the idiom means working as one

explanation.surface: Sports pundits describe a match while one is sharp-tongued.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means working as a prostitute, which is what tart implies.

clue.text: Worked out food component in starter for dinner

parts.note: fat is one of the components of food
in means at home

indicators.note: a starter is the first course, so this takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Identifying an ingredient in the first course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To fathom a puzzle is to understand it, a synonym for working it out.

clue.text: Plant a conifer, vital after devastation

indicators.note: devastation wrecks the words, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener plants a tree that was vital after a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The popular houseplant Saintpaulia, from East Africa, is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Against including rude word to become more vulgar

indicators.note: including means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
arse is a vulgar British word for backside

explanation.surface: Objecting to swearing that makes things cruder.
explanation.definitionFit: To coarsen is to grow rougher or cruder, a synonym for becoming more vulgar.

clue.text: Song balefully arranged with two successive notes missing

indicators.note: arranged means the remaining letters are set out in a new order
missing means these letters are absent from the word

parts.note: E and F are neighbouring notes of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A gloomy tune arranged with a couple of adjacent notes dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes EF from BALEFULLY to leave BALULLY, then 'arranged' shuffles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle tune sung to send a child to sleep is a type of song.

clue.text: Lacking a part in decision-making to stop plan of action

indicators.note: lacking means the following letter is missing from the word

parts.note: having a say is having a part in making a decision
to stem a flow is to stop it

explanation.surface: Without any say in decisions, someone tries to block a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking a' removes A from SAY to leave SY, and 'to stop' gives STEM, as in stemming a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is an organised method or scheme, much like a plan of action.

clue.text: Blow a pipe

parts.note: a hook is a curving punch in boxing

explanation.surface: Someone is told to play a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant spelling of hookah, the water pipe used for smoking tobacco.

clue.text: Drug this person's got outside university after work

indicators.note: after puts the following pieces behind the abbreviation for work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: got outside means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: this person is the setter, I, and the 's is has, so I'm

explanation.surface: The setter took a drug outside college after his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this person's' is the setter's I'M (I has, contracted), wrapped round U.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic made from poppies is a classic example of a drug.

clue.text: Guns in vessel badly stowed away

indicators.note: stowed away in means put inside, so the second piece goes within the first

parts.note: an artery is a blood vessel
ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: Weapons hidden carelessly in the hold of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is the blood vessel ARTERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Large mounted guns are collectively artillery, so guns serves as a synonym.

clue.text: Water supply trouble? You can get that on yacht

definitions.text: You can get that on yacht

parts.note: the mains is the public supply of water
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A plumbing fault that you might also find aboard a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal sail on a yacht's mainmast is something you find on such a boat.

clue.text: Scholar succeeded before in Paris

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees
avant is French for before

explanation.surface: An academic who did well before, in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A savant is a learned person, a synonym for a scholar.

clue.text: Bully to be affectionate when holding bird

indicators.note: holding means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: to dote is to be lavishly fond
the mina, also myna, is an Asian starling

explanation.surface: A tyrant is told to be kind while clutching a pet bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To dominate is to control others by force, a synonym for bully as a verb.

clue.text: My clue may be worked out in a place of study

indicators.note: worked out here means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: The setter hopes his clue will be solved in a classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle taught at the Lyceum in Athens, so the word means a school or place of learning.
